documents: Meegan Kumar et al. 2022, Glacial Warming in the Eastern Pacific Warm Pool, Geophysical Research Letters 49, e2022GL098830 (published PDF, 10 pages)

entry.evidence: Without data from the central and northern EPWP to compare with these southern sites, we lack a unified understanding of how this region responded to [...]

sequences.source_document: Meegan Kumar et al. 2022, GRL, published PDF

steps.action: Pose the question of how the northern EPWP responded to past climate change, given that existing ETP records come from the equatorial and southern Central American sites.
steps.quote: How representative records from these latitudes are of EPWP [...] .

steps.action: Sample core NH22P at about 1 sample per kyr and measure alkenone concentrations by GC-FID.
steps.quote: concentrations of alkenones were measured with an Agilent 7890 Gas Chromatograph-Flame Ionization Detector

steps.action: Compute UK'37 and convert it to SST with the Bayesian BAYSPLINE calibration, reporting the analytical error in SST units.
steps.quote: then converted to SST using the

steps.action: Build a new age model with BACON from 14C dates (Marine20, local reservoir correction) and benthic d18O tie points to LR04.
steps.quote: generated a new age model for NH22P

steps.action: Analyse CESM1.2 fully coupled LGM and PI simulations and single-forcing GHG and ICE experiments to separate the glacial forcings.
steps.quote: we analyze single-forcing simulations of the LGM also generated with CESM1.2.

steps.action: Check that the coarse-resolution model captures the observed Tehuantepec wind gap pattern and the seasonal growth of the EPWP (Figure S2).
steps.quote: it is sufficient for capturing the basic spatiotemporal pattern of winds and SST associated with the Tehuantepec wind gap

steps.action: Establish that the NH22P record shows recurring warming intervals during globally cool stages, with warming rates correlated to pCO2 and benthic d18O changes.
steps.quote: Elevated SSTs at NH22P were contemporaneous with periods of global cooling

steps.action: Compare NH22P with LPAZ-21P, MD02-2529, ME0005A-43JC and ODP 846, finding no sawtooth pattern and no coherence with the southern EPWP cores.
steps.quote: there is no coherency in the pattern of SST evolution at NH22P and southern EPWP cores

steps.action: Compare the proxy LGM warming with PMIP models, including CESM1.2, which simulate cooling of 2.6 to 3.3 C but attenuated cooling in the EPWP.
steps.quote: Elevated LGM SST at site NH22P is not captured by the Paleoclimate Modeling Intercomparison Project (PMIP)

steps.action: Name three candidate drivers of the attenuated cooling: ice sheet expansion, lower GHG, and orbital insolation changes.
steps.quote: can conceivably be linked to the three major external climatic forcings operating during glacial times

steps.action: Derive from the ICE experiment that ice sheets intensify the trade winds and gap jets, causing downwelling in the northern EPWP and the least glacial cooling there.
steps.quote: The ICE simulation shows ice sheet forcing intensified northeasterly trade winds

steps.action: Test the reduced-upwelling mechanism against independent NH22P Corg and biogenic opal records; correlations are low and possibly confounded by nutrients and ventilation.
steps.quote: correlations between SST and Corg and biogenic opal are low

steps.action: Keep reduced upwelling under ice sheet forcing as a partial contributor that explains neither the full magnitude nor the periodicity.
steps.quote: The model data nevertheless provide evidence for some contribution of reduced upwelling to glacial SST warming at NH22P

steps.action: Derive from the GHG experiment a cooler cold tongue, an enhanced meridional gradient, stronger summer southwesterlies and a northward ITCZ that reduce latent heat flux over the EPWP.
steps.quote: Our GHG simulation results are consistent with these prior studies

steps.action: Keep GHG forcing as a secondary contributor to the attenuated cooling, weaker than ice sheet forcing.
steps.quote: Thus, GHGs likely also contributed to reduced cooling in the EPWP

steps.action: Exclude GHG and ice sheet forcing as the driver of the regular recurrence of the warming events.
steps.quote: there must be a more periodic driver than GHG or ice sheet forcing

steps.action: Run a Lomb-Scargle spectral analysis that finds power near the obliquity and precession bands, with significance not evaluable for a 144 kyr record.
steps.quote: found power near both the obliquity (41 kyr) and precession (23 kyr) bands

steps.action: Set out the orbital rivals from published theory: obliquity through the thermocline, the autumnal-equinox ocean dynamical thermostat, and vernal-equinox shortwave heating.
steps.quote: Clement et al. (1996) described the ocean dynamical thermostat mechanism

steps.action: Reject obliquity as the full explanation because it does not account for the smaller warming intervals in MIS 3b and 5b.
steps.quote: this mechanism does not explain the smaller warming intervals that occur during MIS 3b and 5b

steps.action: Reject the autumnal-equinox thermostat because the autumnal insolation maxima do not coincide with the warming intervals.
steps.quote: autumnal equinox insolation maxima do not coincide with the NH22P SST warming intervals

steps.action: Compare the timing of vernal equinox insolation maxima with the NH22P warming intervals and find good agreement (Figure 2).
steps.quote: There is good agreement between the timing of vernal equinox insolation maxima and SST warming at NH22P

steps.action: Keep precession through spring shortwave heating, with a nonlinear and asymmetric response, as the plausible pacing mechanism.
steps.quote: it seems plausible that precession is driving the recurrence of these warming events during the last glacial period

steps.action: Refine the account so that, given no warming at Termination II despite high spring insolation, orbital warming requires a glacial background, and posit a synergistic layered ice, GHG and orbital mechanism.
steps.quote: we posit that the glacial warming events observed in NH22P resulted from a synergistic response to ice sheet, GHG, and orbital forcing

steps.action: Compare the result with the simplified-model result of Timmermann et al. (2007) that precession paces the ETP meridional SST gradient.
steps.quote: This proxy evidence confirms the results of Timmermann, Lorenz, et al. (2007)

steps.action: Attribute the model's failure to produce absolute warming to coarse resolution and known CESM1.2 Tehuantepec easterly and double-ITCZ biases, rather than revising the proxy claim.
steps.quote: The lack of glacial warming in the EPWP in our model simulations may be due to an insufficient resolution

steps.action: Keep the headline claim that ice and GHG forcing reduced the WES feedback, priming the EPWP, and that spring insolation maxima paced the warming spikes.
steps.quote: Direct shortwave heating during spring insolation maxima is the most likely driver of the precessional pacing

tree.answer: Warming repeats in each globally cool MIS, at roughly precessional pacing
Partly: upwelling proxies inconclusive, model misses absolute warming, spectral significance untested
Layered ice and GHG priming plus vernal insolation pacing kept as most likely
Not documented; no review file supplied

end.claim: Combined ice sheet and GHG forcing reduced the wind-evaporation-SST feedback in the EPWP, priming it for glacial warming, and direct shortwave heating during spring insolation maxima most likely paced the warming spikes at NH22P.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the new 144 kyr alkenone record from NH22P, which documents warming during global cool periods, there would be no phenomenon to explain and no constraint on the rival forcings.

gates.evidence: The core was analysed to fill a spatial data gap (p. 2), not to test a stated hypothesis. The orbital rivals faced a timing test the vernal mechanism could have failed (pp. 6-7), but spectral significance was not evaluated (p. 6). The ice and GHG mechanisms rest on simulations that fail to reproduce the warming (p. 7). Nothing is reported as fixed in advance.

imports.item: Lomb-Scargle periodogram for unevenly sampled series
Gas chromatograph with flame ionization detector

novelty_claims.quote: our SST reconstruction from NH22P is the first documentation of repeated intervals of glacial SST warming during each of the globally cool MIS

limits: Coded from the published PDF only. Supporting Information (Text S1, Figures S1-S6) was not supplied, so the methods checks and the spectral result are taken from main-text descriptions. No review file was supplied; the acknowledgments name two reviewers whose comments improved the manuscript, but what changed cannot be coded. The CESM simulations were generated in the coauthors' earlier work (Tierney et al. 2020; Windler et al. 2020); they are coded as analysed here (S, new), although running them is inherited. Inference: age-model uncertainty is not reported as propagated into the timing comparison with insolation. The claim rests on a single core, which the authors acknowledge. Sub-claims: (1) the glacial warming phenomenon at NH22P has status estimate_with_resolution (median and 1-2 sigma bands; analytical error ±0.14 to ±0.5 C). (2) Ice sheet and GHG attenuation of cooling has status best_explanation, supported by simulations that do not reproduce absolute warming. (3) The reduced-upwelling contribution is partial and its proxy test is inconclusive. (4) Precessional pacing has status best_explanation; the spectral power is not well resolved and its significance is untested. (5) The implication of a more northerly ITCZ is speculative.

disagreements.target: PMIP LGM model ensemble including CESM1.2 (Kageyama et al., 2021)
disagreements.support: The proxy shows LGM warming at NH22P where the models simulate 2.6-3.3 C of cooling; the authors attribute the mismatch to model resolution and known biases.
disagreements.quote: Elevated LGM SST at site NH22P is not captured by the Paleoclimate Modeling Intercomparison Project (PMIP)

disagreements.target: Previous synthesis studies using MD02-2529 and ME0005A-43JC as EPWP representatives (Kienast et al., 2013; McGee et al., 2014)
disagreements.support: The NH22P record shows no coherence with these southern cores, questioning whether they represent the whole EPWP.
disagreements.quote: which have been used as representatives of the EPWP in previous synthesis studies

disagreements.target: Ocean dynamical thermostat via autumnal equinox insolation (Clement et al., 1996)
disagreements.support: Autumnal equinox insolation maxima do not coincide with the warming intervals in Figure 2.
disagreements.quote: [...] unlikely that this mechanism underlies the 23 kyr frequency identified in our spectral results

disagreements.target: Interpretation of NH22P Corg and opal as upwelling indicators (Ganeshram & Pedersen, 1998)
disagreements.support: Low correlations with SST, and glacial changes in ventilation and nutrients, may confound the upwelling signal.
disagreements.quote: As these indicators are also sensitive to nutrient concentrations

disagreements.target: Global mean energetic frameworks for ITCZ position (Atwood et al., 2020; Boos & Korty, 2016)
disagreements.support: The regional SST pattern and GHG simulation imply a more northerly glacial ITCZ in the ETP.
disagreements.quote: which may have been more northerly in the ETP than suggested by global mean energetic frameworks

alternatives_considered.chosen: Vernal equinox insolation and direct shortwave heating as the pacing mechanism
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Obliquity forcing via the thermocline and La Niña-like SST; the autumnal equinox ocean dynamical thermostat (Clement et al., 1996)
alternatives_considered.reason: Obliquity misses the MIS 3b and 5b intervals; autumnal maxima do not coincide with the warming; vernal maxima agree in timing

alternatives_considered.chosen: Layered effect of ice sheet, GHG and orbital forcing, with ice sheets dominant over GHG
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Ice sheet forcing alone; GHG forcing alone; orbital forcing alone
alternatives_considered.reason: Single-forcing simulations show that both attenuate cooling but neither gives periodicity; GHG causes more ETP cooling than ICE

alternatives_considered.chosen: Model evidence for some reduced-upwelling contribution
alternatives_considered.alternatives: NH22P Corg and biogenic opal upwelling proxies
alternatives_considered.reason: Proxy correlations are low and the proxies may be confounded by nutrient and ventilation changes
